dasn't: dialect for 'dare not'; did not dare
bymeby: dialect for 'by and by'; before long
by-and-by: before long; eventually, after a while
ransomed: dialect for 'ransomed'; freed by paying a price
sot: old word for 'set' or 'sat' in a stubborn way
canoe: narrow light boat paddled with a paddle
ferry: boat carrying people and goods across a river
ferry-boat: boat carrying people and goods across a river
hair-ball: a ball of hair found in an animal's stomach
wadding: soft material used to pack gunpowder into a gun
ambuscade: old word for an ambush; a hidden attack
shot-tower: tall tower where lead shot was dropped to form pellets
stile: steps over a fence or wall for people to climb
gourd: hard-shelled fruit used as a container
quicksilver: old name for mercury, a liquid metal
sun-bonnet: bonnet with a wide brim to shade the face
snake-skin: the shed skin of a snake
cowhide: the leather made from a cow's skin; a whip
stove-pipe: metal pipe carrying smoke from a stove
clasp-knife: folding knife with a blade that locks
whisky-jug: jug used to carry or hold whisky
five-center: a five-cent coin or item costing five cents
wood-flat: flat-bottomed boat used for carrying wood
hatchet: small axe with a short handle
awful: very great; extremely, in an old sense
considerable: a fair amount; quite a lot
lightning: bright flash of electricity during a storm
dressed: in old use, cleaned or prepared; here, clothed
crawling: moving slowly on hands and knees
tanyard: yard where hides are soaked and tanned
shooting: firing guns or shooting at targets
sundown: sunset; the time the sun goes down
sun-up: sunrise; the time the sun comes up
lookout: a person who keeps watch for danger
stairs: steps leading from one floor to another
honey: a term of affection used to address someone
calico: cheap cotton cloth with small printed patterns
curled: wound into rings or bent into curves
sucked: drew in with the mouth; drank by sucking
quality: people of high social rank; the upper class
plunkety-plunk: making a repeated plucking or plinking sound
string: a long thin cord or line of things
masks: coverings worn over the face to disguise it
scratch: a line or mark made by a sharp object; a scrape
